reviews.title: Pro That Isn't So Much Pro
reviews.text: Pro that basically gives nothing in return, love how I waisted money on this back then which is why ai never paid this company anything more than that.

reviews.title: Incorrect advertisement
reviews.text: You buy the pro version and they say hurricane tracker is available in CarPlay. It’s not even available on the iPhone unless you buy a one year subscription after you pay for the pro version. False advertisement!

reviews.title: Disappointing not accurate
reviews.text: In comparing with two other apps this app was horrible at displaying approaching thunderstorms. A good example was yesterday. Looking at two other apps a storm was approaching and we were in the yellow and red. This app showed nothing even close to us. The other two apps were absolutely correct! We got a downpour and while we were getting the weather this app still displayed nothing close to us. Note: I did pay for Pro upon downloading the app. My advice is try before spending extra maybe the radar is better in your area. This is no use to me.

reviews.title: Hazardous weather warnings
reviews.text: I keep getting hazardous weather warnings, multiple times a day, every day. Today so far, before noon, I got two warnings, that threaten multiple waves of severe thunderstorms, tornado, hail, wind gusts up to 70mph, and squalls, and yet I see nothing on radar.  Hot yes, it is hot here, but really?  Weather warnings of biblical proportions?  You should understand that accuracy in these warnings is as important as daily forecasting, and repeated imminent threats that are not valid will cause users to ignore the valid ones.  This is not urging me to use the app more frequently, but causing me to look elsewhere for something that does not remind me of Chicken Little.  Daily forecasting is quite good, and lots of choices for details.  It’s also nice to be able to check the weather for family across the country.

reviews.title: Why does the app need to know my precise location?
reviews.text: When I try to use this app with CarPlay, it says it needs to know my precise location and won’t let me use the app. You don’t need to know my exact location - you only need to know the location of where I want to know what the weather is doing. I think MyRadar is double dipping and probably selling your location info to 3rd party’s. Otherwise fix this ridiculous setting requirement. No one likes a nosey app.

reviews.title: It’s never correct
reviews.text: This app is always wrong.  I have never experienced it to be correct. It’s a total waste of money. Beyond disappointed.

reviews.title: Not very accurate
reviews.text: The radar isn’t showing any rain it’s pouring outside.

reviews.title: App sells third parties your precise location
reviews.text:
I’ve been a user of this app for years but selling user location data is unacceptable.  Please stop selling the location data of your users. 

This is a snippet from the MyRadar privacy policy:

“NOTICE: We may sell your sensitive personal data. In particular, we sell precise geolocation data, along with other related data, to the below third parties.”

You’re even headquartered in my hometown, I used to drive by the building and feel a sense of pride, now I feel only shame and embarrassment.

reviews.title: scam
reviews.text: Locks carplay behind outrageous subscription fee even after I paid for the full price app.

reviews.title: Always bad forecasts
reviews.text: The presentation is great, except the data that it gives is always so far from accurate it defeats the purpose.   Not worth the money.   Easy pass.

reviews.title: Not a fan of latest update
reviews.text: What the hell is up with these disappearing radar icons. I don't need a bunch of distractions when I look at the radar I don't care that they disappear after a few seconds every time you move the radar screen they reappear and then you have to wait for them to disappear this is extremely distracting especially in areas like DFW that has several of these rarely used radars.  There should've been an option to display or not to display those. Poorly thought out update

reviews.title: INSURANCE SPY APP
reviews.text:
This app has a gorgeous hi-res display.  
Unfortunately they do sell your driving behavior to the insurance industry with the GPS and your contact information.  These “partners” may include LexisNexis, Insurance  Information Exchange and the 3 credit bureaus.  

There is no such thing as an app without costs.  

Minimally DO NOT give this app access to your GPS.

reviews.title: Scam compared to the free version
reviews.text: This was a paid version of the app that unlocks most of its features but keeps some behind a subscription. Now after recent updates, there is no difference between this app and the free version, and everything that I originally paid for is now behind a monthly subscription paywall. This is unfair to everyone who originally purchased these features. One of the most important features is “per station radar” which has always been included in this paid version but is not anymore.

reviews.title: Confused
reviews.text: I paid for this app yet support can’t reply to my request about explaining the colors used in the forecast view.  Very sad.

reviews.title: Useless In Storms
reviews.text: This app dies and gives ZERO updates to the radar or warnings in storm scenarios. Restarted the phone, cleared every cache I could find, severe weather conditions and nothing from this apps radar or notifications. Absolute failure!

reviews.title: Pestering Pop ups
reviews.text: Been a user of this app for years, but it’s time to move on. I’m tired of the constant pop up wanting users to invest in company.

reviews.title: Awesome on iPhone, what happened here?
reviews.text: Would be really nice if it were even one tenth the app it is on iPhone. On macOS 26.3 and 26.4 Beta 1 the widget cannot maintain a location so goes blank. This is on a MacbBook Pro M5 so it is mobile. What happened? Features? Quality? Please fix. This should be a 5 star app. It boggles the mind.

reviews.title: Usually wrong
reviews.text: For this to be a paid app and they are advertising people to invest in it, the weather is never correct. Apple’s weather app is more reliable than this an they’re free.

reviews.title: Bug report
reviews.text:
The new update has a disorienting animation when sliding down the forecast bar to show the full forecast. Not sure why this changed 

Watches/warnings notification sounds are now just the default apple sound I assign instead of the custom weather radio sound I used to hear on this app. How to fix? Can we have custom sounds for watches vs warnings?

reviews.title: App privacy collecting health info?
reviews.text:
The app now collects immense personal info, including health info on my iphone. I paid for this app.  Whh is it selling my personal info?

I’ve  had My Radar Pr for several years, and use nothing else for radar.  Excellent local weather with rain, storm, and flood warnings.  I added hurricane tracking promptly.  Many features such as air quality, winds, etc., all of which are “layers” that can be turned on or off.  

I note that I purchased after using the free version for a few months, along with competitive versions.  None were nearly as good as My Radar.  The Pro version is worth the lack of ads.  I also note the constant improvement over the years.  I’ll have no other.

reviews.title: Quality is gone.. no radar last few days
reviews.text:
They have one job to do, provide reliable, high-quality radar. But alas, it seems their attention has gone in other directions, and I can’t even get the radar feed for the record-breaking winter storm over the last couple of days. So I had to rely on my Windy app, which is so much more valuable and provides so much more in weather.

And no, I don’t wanna invest in an inferior, already outdated product.  I mean Sheesh.. contiipopups asking to invest, give me a break!

reviews.title: Radar Pro you went from 5 stars to 1
reviews.text: I will delete this app forever - why?   I just found out that if you subscribe to the my-drive feature that is sold to help you drive better and keep logs of your drives and be helpful - that is the sales pitch.  If you sign up you get a legal page, unless you read it completely, you will not be aware that you data gets shipped of to databrokers with a unique id to your phone, not your name, but you phone is tagged.   One of the companies apparently they sell data to is Arity owned by Allstate.  Here is the problem, you are paying for that feature to be turned on, and then radar pro makes more money selling your driving data…. I appeal to the company to stop this practice and charge more upfront but not trick people.    Reading the legal disclaimers does not occur and to not explain it in the sales pitch that you are going to consent to data mining is wrong.
